title: Facebook’s Plan to Police the Truth

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简讯

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《Dealbook》的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 Dealbook 峰会现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的一些领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on
sentences.zh: 我们将于 11 月 18 日

sentences.en: November 18th.
sentences.zh: 在 nytimes.com 上免费直播部分精选访谈，供任何人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并免费阅读我们所有的 A 类新闻一个月。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily News.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: The last time Facebook was under intense scrutiny was when Mark Zuckerberg had to defend himself in front of Congress.
sentences.zh: 脸书上次受到密切审视，还是马克·扎克伯格不得不去国会为自己辩护的时候。

sentences.en: Now, he's bringing scrutiny back on Facebook with his plan to police the truth.
sentences.zh: 现在，他正通过自己管理真相的计划，让脸书重新回到聚光灯下。

sentences.en: It's Friday, July 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 7 月 20 日，星期五。

sentences.en: We welcome everyone to today's hearing on Facebook's social media privacy and the use and abuse of data.
sentences.zh: 我们欢迎各位出席今天的听证会，讨论脸书的社交媒体隐私以及数据的利用和滥用问题。

sentences.en: So, in April, we saw Mark Zuckerberg testifying on Capitol
sentences.zh: 所以在 4 月份，我们看到马克·扎克伯格在国会

sentences.en: Hill about Cambridge Analytica, this data firm that had gotten illicit user data and was using it to help, among other people, the Trump campaign.
sentences.zh: 山作证，内容关于剑桥分析公司——这家数据公司获取了非法的用户数据，并利用这些数据协助特朗普竞选团队等对象。

sentences.en: Kevin Roos covers technology for the Times.
sentences.zh: 凯文·罗斯负责《时报》的科技报道。

sentences.en: We didn't take a broad enough view of our responsibility, and that was a big mistake.
sentences.zh: 我们对自身责任的审视还不够全面，这是一个重大的错误。

sentences.en: And it was my mistake.
sentences.zh: 这也是我的错误。

sentences.en: And I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 对此我深表歉意。

sentences.en: And what resulted from those hearings was sort of a parade of grievances.
sentences.zh: 这些听证会产生的结果，可以说是各种不满的游行。

sentences.en: You had all kinds of issues coming up.
sentences.zh: 你遇到了各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: Well, Mr. Zuckerberg, I will say there are a great many Americans who I think are deeply concerned that Facebook and other tech companies are engaged in
sentences.zh: 嗯，扎克伯格先生，我要说的是，有相当多的美国人深感担忧，他们认为脸书和其他科技公司正在参与

sentences.en: a pervasive pattern of bias and political censorship.
sentences.zh: 一种普遍存在的偏见和政治审查模式。

sentences.en: I mean, you have people who think Facebook is biased against one political party or the other.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些人认为脸书对某个政党有偏见。

sentences.en: We've seen how foreign actors are abusing social media platforMs. You have people who think that Facebook is too easily exploited by Russian information
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到外国势力是如何滥用社交媒体平台的。有些人认为脸书太容易被俄罗斯情报

sentences.en: operations and other foreign influence campaigns.
sentences.zh: 活动和其他外国影响力行动所利用。

sentences.en: One of the key issues here is, is Facebook too powerful?
sentences.zh: 这里的一个关键问题是，脸书是不是太强大了？

sentences.en: Are you too powerful?
sentences.zh: 你们是不是太强大了？

sentences.en: And then you have people who just don't think that Facebook is capable of regulating itself, who think that this company has been allowed to grow to this enormous size
sentences.zh: 然后有些人只是觉得脸书没有能力自我监管，他们认为这家公司在几乎没有什么监督的情况下长得如此庞大

sentences.en: with very little oversight and that now they should have a little more scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们应该接受更多的审视。

sentences.en: So this concludes today's hearing.
sentences.zh: 今天的听证会到此结束。

sentences.en: Thanks to all the witnesses for attending.
sentences.zh: 感谢所有出席的证人。

sentences.en: The hearing is adjourned.
sentences.zh: 听证会休会。

sentences.en: So after these hearings, Facebook embarks on this kind of corporate makeover.
sentences.zh: 所以在这些听证会之后，脸书开始了一场企业大改造。

sentences.en: It meets with lawmakers.
sentences.zh: 它与议员会面。

sentences.en: It expands its fact-checking prograMs. It opens an independent investigation led by a former senator into whether
sentences.zh: 它扩大了事实核查项目。它由一位前参议员牵头，开启了一项独立调查，以查明

sentences.en: Facebook is biased against conservatives.
sentences.zh: 脸书是否存在对保守派的偏见。

sentences.en: And most importantly and most visibly, it takes out a very large ad campaign.
sentences.zh: 最重要、最引人注目的是，它开展了一场非常大型的广告宣传活动。

sentences.en: We came here for the friends.
sentences.zh: 我们来这里是为了找朋友。

sentences.en: And we got to know the friends of our friends.
sentences.zh: 我们还认识了朋友的朋友。

sentences.en: Then our old friends from middle school, our mom, our ex, and our boss joined forces to wish us happy birthday.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们初中的老朋友、我们的妈妈、前任和老板联手祝我们生日快乐。

sentences.en: And we discovered our uncle used to play in a band and realized he was young once too.
sentences.zh: 我们发现叔叔以前玩过乐队，也意识到他曾经年轻过。

sentences.en: And we found others just like us.
sentences.zh: 我们找到了和我们一样的人。

sentences.en: And just like that, we felt a little less alone.
sentences.zh: 就这样，我们觉得自己不那么孤独了。

sentences.en: But then something happened.
sentences.zh: 但后来发生了一些事。

sentences.en: We had to deal with spam, clickbait, fake news, and data misuse.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不应对垃圾信息、点击诱饵、假新闻和数据滥用。

sentences.en: That's going to change.
sentences.zh: 这种情况将会改变。

sentences.en: From now on, Facebook will do more to keep you safe and protect your privacy.
sentences.zh: 从现在开始，脸书将采取更多措施确保您的安全并保护您的隐私。

sentences.en: So we can all get back to what made Facebook good in the first place.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能回到最初让脸书变得美好的事物上来。

sentences.en: Friends.
sentences.zh: 朋友。

sentences.en: Because when this place does what it was built for,
sentences.zh: 因为当这个地方发挥其建立时的作用时，

sentences.en: then we all get a little closer.
sentences.zh: 我们之间的距离就会更近一点。

sentences.en: So the overall message is, something bad happened.
sentences.zh: 所以总的信息是，发生了不好的事情。

sentences.en: We're going to fix it for you.
sentences.zh: 我们会为你解决。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then in the last few weeks, they've started inviting reporters into their office to tell them how they're going to do this.
sentences.zh: 然后在过去的几周里，他们开始邀请记者去他们的办公室，告诉他们将如何做到这一点。

sentences.en: Did you go?
sentences.zh: 你去了吗？

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我去了。

sentences.en: Last week, there was a group of reporters that went to Facebook's office.
sentences.zh: 上周，有一群记者去了脸书的办公室。

sentences.en: They're little, you know, appetizers and drinks.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有小吃和饮料。

sentences.en: And then we sit down around a big conference room table, and they play a video.
sentences.zh: 然后我们围坐在一张大型会议室桌子旁，他们播放了一段视频。

sentences.en: Facebook and other social media sites are being criticized for not doing enough to stop bogus stories that seem to dominate the election cycle.
sentences.zh: 脸书和其他社交媒体网站正受到批评，被指责在阻止似乎主导了选举周期的虚假故事方面做得不够。

sentences.en: It's a 12-minute documentary that they've made called Facing Facts.
sentences.zh: 这是他们制作的一部名为《直面事实》的 12 分钟纪录片。

sentences.en: It's basically their version of a chronicle of how they approach false news and misinformation on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是他们记录自己如何在脸书上处理虚假新闻和错误信息的一种方式。

sentences.en: For a time, we felt our responsibility was mostly around just trying to help organize that information that you, in some sense, had asked to see.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，我们觉得我们的责任主要在于试图帮助整理那些你在某种程度上要求查看的信息。

sentences.en: And it has interviews with people on their teaMs.
sentences.zh: 其中包含对其团队成员的采访。

sentences.en: One of the challenges in misinformation is that there is no one consensus or source for truth.
sentences.zh: 错误信息面临的挑战之一是，对于真相没有单一的共识或来源。

sentences.en: It shows them thinking through and sort of trying to figure out what is or isn't false news.
sentences.zh: 它展示了他们深入思考并试图弄清楚什么是或不是虚假新闻的过程。

sentences.en: The truth has this unfortunate aspect to it that sometimes it is not aligned with your desires.
sentences.zh: 真相有一个不幸的方面，那就是有时它并不符合你的愿望。

sentences.en: It is not aligned with what you have invested in, what you would like.
sentences.zh: 它不符合你投入精力的方向，不符合你的喜好。

sentences.en: Facebook has had rules forever about what you can and can't put on its platform.
sentences.zh: 对于什么可以在其平台上发布、什么不可以，脸书一直都有规定。

sentences.en: They've had rules against nudity.
sentences.zh: 他们有反对色情内容的规定。

sentences.en: They've had rules against graphic violence.
sentences.zh: 他们有反对血腥暴力的规定。

sentences.en: They've had rules against harassment.
sentences.zh: 他们有反对骚扰的规定。

sentences.en: But the one category that they have resisted wading into until pretty recently is this idea of what's true and what's false and what's deliberate misinformation
sentences.zh: 但直到最近，他们一直拒绝涉足的一个领域是：什么是真的，什么是假的，什么是蓄意的错误信息，

sentences.en: and what's people just being wrong on the Internet.
sentences.zh: 以及什么是人们在互联网上单纯犯错。

sentences.en: And why have they resisted that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要抵制这一点？

sentences.en: Why is that the last holdout?
sentences.zh: 为什么这是最后的坚守？

sentences.en: Well, because how the hell do you build something that can accurately and completely
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为你怎么能建造一个能够准确、彻底地

sentences.en: rid a platform of misinformation that has 2 billion people on it?
sentences.zh: 清除拥有 20 亿用户的平台上的错误信息的系统呢？

sentences.en: And frankly, it's also where they face the most political danger.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，这也是他们面临最大政治危险的地方。

sentences.en: Because as we know, our political climate is not dominated by people who agree on a single set of facts.
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们所知，我们的政治气候并不是由在单一事实集上达成一致的人主导的。

sentences.en: And it's basically their attempt to say, look, this is really hard.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是他们的尝试，意在说明：看，这真的很难。

sentences.en: We're dedicated to finding our way through it, but it might take us a while, and it's going to involve some really important and hard trade-offs.
sentences.zh: 我们致力于寻找出路，但这可能需要一段时间，并且会涉及一些非常重要且艰难的权衡。

sentences.en: One famous example of this is the photo of the Seattle Seahawks supposedly burning an American flag in a locker room.
sentences.zh: 一个著名的例子是西雅图海鹰队涉嫌在更衣室里焚烧美国国旗的照片。

sentences.en: So they had a story about a Photoshopped picture of the Seattle Seahawks burning an American flag, which never happened, but the Photoshopped picture went viral on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们报道了一个关于西雅图海鹰队焚烧美国国旗的修图照片的故事，这从未发生过，但这张修图照片在脸书上广为流传。

sentences.en: One of the cases of ideologically motivated misinformation was a story of an undocumented immigrant.
sentences.zh: 意识形态驱动的错误信息的案例之一是一个关于无证移民的故事。

sentences.en: They had a report that was about an illegal immigrant who allegedly committed arson, which was not true.
sentences.zh: 他们的一篇报道称一名非法移民涉嫌纵火，这不是真的。

sentences.en: These are things that were explicitly designed and architected to be viral.
sentences.zh: 这些都是明确设计和架构为病毒式传播的内容。

sentences.en: These are the hoaxes of the world.
sentences.zh: 这些是世界上的恶作剧。

sentences.en: These are things like Pizzagate.
sentences.zh: 这些东西就像披萨门。

sentences.en: This is just false news.
sentences.zh: 这只是假新闻。

sentences.en: I mean, all this anger and frustration, they're basically saying, look at what we actually have to deal with every single day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有的这些愤怒和挫败感，他们基本上是在说，看看我们每天实际上必须应对的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's pretty remarkable how little we know about how Facebook makes decisions,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为非常引人注目的是，鉴于脸书统治着世界上很大一部分人的言论和媒体消费，

sentences.en: given that they sort of govern the speech and media consumption of a big chunk of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们对他们如何做出决策却知之甚少。

sentences.en: This was really one of the first times that we've actually been able to see how they make these decisions.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我们第一次能够真正看到他们是如何做出这些决策的。

sentences.en: Once we were able to define the tactic or the problem area, we're able to make more progress on it.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们能够定义战术或问题领域，我们就能够在上面取得更多进展。

sentences.en: And it was a very controlled and sort of sanitized version of that.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常受控且经过某种程度净化的版本。

sentences.en: But it did show some of the thinking behind what they eventually put into policies.
sentences.zh: 但它确实展示了他们最终纳入政策的想法背后的某些思考。

sentences.en: Bad behavior is using tactics like spamming to try to spread a message.
sentences.zh: 不良行为是使用垃圾信息等战术来试图传播信息。

sentences.en: So this documentary is meant to say it's going to be very hard to do this,
sentences.zh: 所以这部纪录片的意思是，这会非常难做，

sentences.en: but we're finally going to develop a system for misinformation that gets at this incredibly thorny question of the nature of truth.
sentences.zh: 但我们最终要为错误信息开发一个系统，来解决关于真相本质这个极其棘手的问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We have to get this right, not just for our platform, but for the community of people that we serve around the world.
sentences.zh: 我们必须把这一点做好，不仅是为了我们的平台，也是为了我们在世界各地服务的社群。

sentences.en: And what do you make of this presentation inside Facebook's offices?
sentences.zh: 你对脸书办公室里的这场演示作何感想？

sentences.en: How do the reporters in the room respond to it?
sentences.zh: 房间里的记者们是如何反应的？

sentences.en: It got pretty contentious pretty faSt.
sentences.zh: 情况很快就变得颇具争议。

sentences.en: I mean, I think after the video ended...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想在视频结束后……

sentences.en: Hi, Kevin Roos from The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是《纽约时报》的凯文·罗斯。

sentences.en: I asked a question about, well, in the video, I thought that was a very interesting video.
sentences.zh: 我提出了一个问题，嗯，在视频里，我认为那是一个非常有趣的视频。

sentences.en: Thank you for showing it.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们播放它。

sentences.en: Some of the examples that were used in the video, like the Pizzagate example, the Wine County arsonist story,
sentences.zh: 视频中用到的一些例子，比如披萨门例子、酒乡纵火犯的故事、

sentences.en: the fake photo of the Seahawks burning, those came from, in some cases, organizations with sort of millions of Facebook followers.
sentences.zh: 海鹰队焚烧旗帜的假照片，在某些情况下，它们来自拥有数百万脸书粉丝的组织。

sentences.en: One was Infowars, one was Breitbart, one was a group called Vets for Trump.
sentences.zh: 一个是 Infowars，一个是布赖特巴特新闻网，一个是名为“特朗普老兵”的组织。

sentences.en: Have you taken any action against those specific organizations that you called out in your video?
sentences.zh: 你们对视频中点名的那些特定组织采取了什么行动吗？

sentences.en: And what is the response from the Facebook officials standing near you?
sentences.zh: 站在你附近的脸书官员作何回应？

sentences.en: Well, they said, basically, that pages that repeatedly put out false news, pages that repeatedly violate their guidelines,
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们基本上说，一再发布假新闻的页面，一再违反其准则的页面，

sentences.en: pages that are threatening or harassing people, will be penalized.
sentences.zh: 威胁或骚扰人们的页面，将会受到惩罚。

sentences.en: They will be demoted, essentially made less visible to their followers.
sentences.zh: 它们将被降级，本质上使其对粉丝的可见度降低。

sentences.en: They're kind of buried.
sentences.zh: 它们有点被埋没了。

sentences.en: Yeah, buried, and, you know, their distribution will be cut, in Facebook's words.
sentences.zh: 对，被埋没，你知道的，用脸书的话说，它们的传播范围会被削减。

sentences.en: Uh, Oliver Darcy from CNN.
sentences.zh: 呃，来自 CNN 的奥利弗·达西。

sentences.en: And then a CNN reporter raised his hand and said, well...
sentences.zh: 然后 CNN 的一名记者举手说，嗯……

sentences.en: I'm kind of curious, like, Facebook is really devoted to finding fake news and false news.
sentences.zh: 我有点好奇，比如脸书真的致力于寻找假新闻和虚假新闻。

sentences.en: How does Infowars have an account on your website?
sentences.zh: 为什么 Infowars 在你们的网站上还有一个账号？

sentences.en: What about Infowars?
sentences.zh: 那 Infowars 呢？

sentences.en: I mean, if you are so dedicated to combating misinformation on Facebook, why do you let this page exist that has repeatedly spread conspiracy theories,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你如此致力于打击脸书上的错误信息，为什么你要让这个一再散布阴谋论、

sentences.en: things about Pizzagate, things about the Parkland shooting, about Sandy Hook before that?
sentences.zh: 关于披萨门的事情、关于帕克兰枪击案的事情、在此之前关于桑迪·胡克的事情的页面存在？

sentences.en: Why are they even allowed on the platform at all?
sentences.zh: 为什么甚至允许他们留在平台上？

sentences.en: And what was the response?
sentences.zh: 当时的回应是什么？

sentences.en: The guy who runs News Feed basically says, look, just being false doesn't violate our standards.
sentences.zh: 负责新闻动态的人基本上说，看，仅仅是虚假并不违反我们的标准。

sentences.en: And that Infowars has not violated a rule that would require taking them down.
sentences.zh: 并且 Infowars 并没有违反需要将其下架的规则。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, basically we created Facebook to be a place where different people have different points of view
sentences.zh: 并且他说，你知道的，基本上我们创建脸书是为了成为一个让不同的人拥有不同观点、

sentences.en: and different publishers think about these things differently and we want to respect the diversity of opinion on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 不同的出版商对这些事情有不同看法的地方，我们希望尊重脸书上意见的多元化。

sentences.en: So the meeting wraps up and we all go back to write our stories.
sentences.zh: 所以会议结束了，我们都回去写我们的报道。

sentences.en: And that Infowars question sort of becomes the story of this meeting.
sentences.zh: 而那个关于 Infowars 的问题某种程度上成为了这次会议报道的核心。

sentences.en: Then it generated a sort of groundswell of controversy on both sides that persisted and led up to Monday when...
sentences.zh: 然后它在双方阵营中引发了一股持续存在的争议热潮，并一直持续到周一，当时……

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: We welcome everyone to this morning's hearing on examining the content filtering practices of social media giants.
sentences.zh: 我们欢迎各位出席今天上午关于审查社交媒体巨头内容过滤实践的听证会。

sentences.en: Representatives from Facebook, Twitter and YouTube went to Congress to talk about censorship and moderation on social media.
sentences.zh: 来自脸书、推特和 YouTube 的代表前往国会，讨论社交媒体上的审查和审核问题。

sentences.en: There were lots of questions from lawmakers.
sentences.zh: 议员们提出了很多问题。

sentences.en: Lawmakers on the Democratic side brought up Infowars.
sentences.zh: 民主党阵营的议员提到了 Infowars。

sentences.en: So just to explain what's happened with Infowars because they've made a cottage industry out of this.
sentences.zh: 所以，只是为了解释 Infowars 发生了什么，因为他们把这搞成了一个家庭手工业般的小作坊。

sentences.en: What they do is they deny that these events have happened.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的就是否认这些事件曾经发生过。

sentences.en: Why are they still on Facebook?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们还在脸书上？

sentences.en: We have removed content from the Infowars page to the extent that it's violated our policies.
sentences.zh: 我们已经对“信息战”主页上违反我们政策的内容进行了移除。

sentences.en: They have not reached the threshold at which their entire...
sentences.zh: 它们还没有达到导致其整个……的门槛

sentences.en: What's the threshold?
sentences.zh: 门槛是什么？

sentences.en: It depends, Congressman, on the nature of the violation.
sentences.zh: 这取决于违规的性质，国会议员先生。

sentences.en: So there are sometimes more severe violations and...
sentences.zh: 所以有时会有更严重的违规，并且……

sentences.en: Lawmakers on the right said, why are you censoring sites like Gateway Pundit, which is another sort of right-wing site that traffics in conspiracy theories.
sentences.zh: 右翼议员们表示，你们为什么要审查像“网关专家”这样的网站，这是另一个兜售阴谋论的右翼网站。

sentences.en: It's a matter of congressional record that Gateway Pundit, Mr. Jim Hoft, has introduced information into the record that in the span of time between 2016 and 2018,
sentences.zh: 国会记录显示，“网关专家”的吉姆·霍夫特先生在2016年至2018年期间提交的信息表明，

sentences.en: he saw his Facebook traffic cut by 54%.
sentences.zh: 他的脸书访问量减少了54%。

sentences.en: And could you render an explanation to that for him and for me, Ms. Bickert?
sentences.zh: 比克特女士，你能为他、也为我对此作出解释吗？

sentences.en: Thank you, Congressman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，国会议员。

sentences.en: I can't speak to any one individual's decline in reach or popularity on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我无法对任何个人在脸书上的触达率或受欢迎程度的下降发表评论。

sentences.en: I can say that we do change the way that our newsfeed algorithm works.
sentences.zh: 我只能说我们确实改变了新闻动态算法的工作方式。

sentences.en: The algorithm, basically, it's individualized, and it gives people...
sentences.zh: 该算法基本上是定制的，它为人们提供……

sentences.en: It sorts or ranks content for each individual user based on people that they follow, pages that they follow, groups that they belong to.
sentences.zh: 它根据每个用户关注的人、关注的主页以及加入的小组，对内容进行分类或排名。

sentences.en: So it's an inventory of content that they have chosen.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他们自己选择的内容清单。

sentences.en: This seems to be a pretty clear sign that Facebook really can't win.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个非常明显的信号，表明脸书真的两头不讨好。

sentences.en: It comes up with a system to demote misinformation, to kind of bury it online.
sentences.zh: 它想出了一个系统来降权虚假信息，将其在网上淡化。

sentences.en: And they think it's a good solution.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一个很好的解决方案。

sentences.en: And Democrats say it's not enough.
sentences.zh: 民主党人说这还不够。

sentences.en: Republicans say it's too much.
sentences.zh: 共和党人说这太过分了。

sentences.en: They're improving Facebook's own point that coming up with a system to divine truth is really hard.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰证明了脸书自己的观点：要设计一个系统来辨别真相是非常困难的。

sentences.en: It's hard unless you're willing to make some politically dangerous and unpopular choices.
sentences.zh: 除非你愿意做出一些在政治上危险且不受欢迎的选择，否则这很难。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, it would be very easy for Facebook to say, we're not going to allow people to say that the earth is flat on Facebook,
sentences.zh: 嗯，对脸书来说，要说“我们不允许人们在脸书上说地球是平的”，非常容易，

sentences.en: and we're going to take down any content that says that the earth is flat.
sentences.zh: 并且我们要删除任何说地球是平的内容。

sentences.en: I'm a member of a mid-sized flat earth Facebook group that is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我是一个中型“地平说”脸书群组的成员，这非常有趣。

sentences.en: But...
sentences.zh: 但是……

sentences.en: You are?
sentences.zh: 你是吗？

sentences.en: I am.
sentences.zh: 我是。

sentences.en: You actually think the earth is round, Michael?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，你真的认为地球是圆的吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: No, it's a fascinating corner of Facebook.
sentences.zh: 不，那是脸书一个引人入胜的角落。

sentences.en: I'm there for journalistic purposes, I promise.
sentences.zh: 我出于新闻采访的目的加入的，我保证。

sentences.en: But I think it would be very easy for them to say, that's obviously false.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们要说“这显然是假的”，会非常容易。

sentences.en: We're going to take that down.
sentences.zh: 我们要把它删掉。

sentences.en: And then you would be banned and your pals in that group, gone.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会被封禁，你在那个群组里的伙伴们也会消失。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But when it comes to more sort of politically salient issues, no matter what you do, you're going to make someone angry.
sentences.zh: 但当涉及到更具政治敏感性的问题时，无论你做什么，都会惹恼某些人。

sentences.en: It makes me wonder, how much of Facebook's decision-making in all of this do you think is built around a fear of the politics of this moment
sentences.zh: 这让我怀疑，你认为脸书在这方面做出的决策，有多少是基于对当前政治氛围的恐惧

sentences.en: and the intensity of the political divisions?
sentences.zh: 以及政治分歧的激烈程度？

sentences.en: It seems like we now know that Facebook helped, in many ways, bring us to this moment because of the way social media amplifies divisions.
sentences.zh: 我们现在似乎知道，由于社交媒体放大了分歧，脸书在许多方面推波助澜，把我们带到了这一刻。

sentences.en: And that may have been inadvertent, but it seems like on some level, they're now making decisions based on fear of making it worse by seeming to pick a side.
sentences.zh: 这可能并非本意，但似乎在某种程度上，他们现在的决策是出于一种恐惧：害怕因为显得偏袒某一方而让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: They don't want to be accused of bias.
sentences.zh: 他们不想被指责带有偏见。

sentences.en: That has been one of their guiding principles for the last several years.
sentences.zh: 这是他们过去几年一直遵循的指导原则之一。

sentences.en: And what do you make of that?
sentences.zh: 你对此怎么看？

sentences.en: I think this is a symptom of something larger, which is that Mark Zuckerberg appears to be profoundly uncomfortable with the power that he has.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是更深层问题的一个症状，那就是马克·扎克伯格似乎对自身拥有的权力感到极度不安。

sentences.en: He built a company that swallowed communication and media for much of the world.
sentences.zh: 他建立了一家吞噬了世界上大部分通信和媒体的公司。

sentences.en: And now I think you're seeing him back away from that, saying, I don't want all this power.
sentences.zh: 而现在我认为你看到他在从这种权力中退缩，并说，我不想拥有所有这些权力。

sentences.en: I mean, the problem with ruling the world is then you have to govern the world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，统治世界的麻烦在于，你必须治理世界。

sentences.en: And that's not, it seems like, what he wants to do.
sentences.zh: 而这似乎并不是他想做的事。

sentences.en: Some people feel you are a nation state in a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得在很多方面你就是一个民族国家。

sentences.en: We're not.
sentences.zh: 我们不是。

sentences.en: We're a company.
sentences.zh: 我们是一家公司。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: You know that.
sentences.zh: 你知道这一点的。

sentences.en: You know people think of you in a much more powerful manner, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想你知道人们认为你比这强大得多。

sentences.en: I think we have a lot of responsibility.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们肩负着沉甸甸的责任。

sentences.en: Well, that's kind of a beautiful segue to the real reason why we're talking to you, Kevin, which was this interview that Mark Zuckerberg did with our future colleague Kara Swisher
sentences.zh: 嗯，这正好巧妙地过渡到了我们采访你凯文的真正原因，也就是马克·扎克伯格接受我们未来的同事卡拉·斯韦舍的这次采访，

sentences.en: about Facebook and about misinformation.
sentences.zh: 关于脸书和关于虚假信息。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he has this interview with Kara Swisher at Recode.
sentences.zh: 是的，他和Recode的卡拉·斯韦舍进行了这次采访。

sentences.en: What does that responsibility feel like?
sentences.zh: 这种责任感感觉如何？

sentences.en: Do you think you have understood it?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你理解它吗？

sentences.en: Because there's a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 因为有很多说法。

sentences.en: Someone was saying to me, you can't just pass power along.
sentences.zh: 有人对我说，你不能就这样把权力传递下去。

sentences.en: You have an enormous amount of power.
sentences.zh: 你拥有巨大的权力。

sentences.en: Do you understand that?
sentences.zh: 你明白这一点吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 还是你考虑过这个问题？

sentences.en: Or you don't think you have?
sentences.zh: 或者你认为自己没有权力？

sentences.en: No, I think we have a big responsibility.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为我们有重大的责任。

sentences.en: But I'm not sure what you mean by pass power along.
sentences.zh: 但我不太明白你说的“传递权力”是什么意思。

sentences.en: But I actually think one of the things that we should be trying to do is figure out how to empower and build other institutions around us that are important
sentences.zh: 但我实际上认为，我们应该尝试做的事情之一，是弄清楚如何赋能并建立在我们周围的其他重要机构，

sentences.en: and can help figure out these new issues on the internet.
sentences.zh: 这些机构可以帮助弄清楚互联网上的这些新问题。

sentences.en: And he keeps saying, I think about it as a responsibility.
sentences.zh: 他一直在说，我把这看作是一种责任。

sentences.en: He's very uncomfortable with the idea that he is the most powerful, one of the most powerful people in the world.
sentences.zh: 对于自己是最强大的人之一、世界上最有权势的人之一这种观点，他感到非常不自在。

sentences.en: And he keeps insisting, you know, I want to empower other people.
sentences.zh: 他一直坚持说，你知道，我想赋予其他人权力。

sentences.en: I don't want to be the emperor on the throne.
sentences.zh: 我不想当坐在王位上的皇帝。

sentences.en: I want to give other people the ability to govern their own communities and lives.
sentences.zh: 我想让其他人有能力治理他们自己的社区和生活。

sentences.en: Let's talk about Infowars.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈“信息战”。

sentences.en: Let's use them as the example.
sentences.zh: 让我们以他们为例。

sentences.en: Make the case for keeping them and make the case for not allowing them to be distributed by you.
sentences.zh: 请为保留他们辩护，同时也为不允许他们由你们进行分发辩护。

sentences.en: Kara and Mark start talking about Infowars.
sentences.zh: 卡拉和马克开始谈论“信息战”。

sentences.en: And we feel like our responsibility is to prevent hoaxes from going viral and being widely distributed.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得我们的责任是防止恶作剧病毒式传播并被广泛分发。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So the approach that we've taken to false news is not that, not to say you can't say something wrong on the internet, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们对待假新闻的方法不是那种，不是说你不能在互联网上说错话，对吧？

sentences.en: I think that that would be too extreme.
sentences.zh: 我认为那太极端了。

sentences.en: Everyone gets things wrong, right?
sentences.zh: 每个人都会弄错，对吧？

sentences.en: And if we were taking down people's accounts when they got a few things wrong, then that would be a hard world for giving people a voice and saying that you care about that.
sentences.zh: 如果我们因为人们犯了几次错误就封禁他们的账号，那么对于给予人们发声权以及宣称你关心这一点来说，这将是一个艰难的世界。

sentences.en: But at the same time, I think that we have a responsibility to when you look at, if you look at the top 100 things that are going viral or getting distribution on Facebook
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我认为我们肩负着一种责任：当你审视那些在任何特定一天内，

sentences.en: within any given day, I do think we have a responsibility to make sure that those aren't hoaxes and blatant misinformation.
sentences.zh: 在脸书上病毒式传播或获得大量分发的前100条内容时，我确实认为我们有责任确保这些不是恶作剧和明目张胆的虚假信息。

sentences.en: Kara asked Zuckerberg about Sandy Hook and the massacre that happened there.
sentences.zh: 卡拉就桑迪胡克小学枪击案及其发生的大屠杀询问了扎克伯格。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Sandy Hook didn't happen is not a debate.
sentences.zh: “桑迪胡克事件没有发生”不是一个可以辩论的话题。

sentences.en: It is false.
sentences.zh: 这是假的。

sentences.en: You can't just take that down.
sentences.zh: 你不能就这么把它删掉吗？

sentences.en: I agree that it is false.
sentences.zh: 我同意这是假的。

sentences.en: And this was really sort of Infowars' flagship issue for years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，这实际上算是“信息战”的旗舰议题。

sentences.en: What they were known for was their promoting of a conspiracy theory that Sandy Hook had been a hoax.
sentences.zh: 他们广为人知的是他们宣扬的一种阴谋论，即桑迪胡克枪击案是一场骗局。

sentences.en: And I also think that going to someone who is a victim of Sandy Hook and telling them, hey, no, you're a liar, that is harassment and we actually will take that down.
sentences.zh: 而且我也认为，去找一个桑迪胡克事件的受害者并告诉他们，嘿，不，你是个骗子，那是骚扰，我们实际上会把那样的内容删掉。

sentences.en: But overall, you know, I mean, let's take this a little closer to home, right?
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，你知道，我的意思是，让我们把这个话题说得更贴近实际一些，好吗？

sentences.en: So I'm Jewish.
sentences.zh: 所以我是犹太人。

sentences.en: And then he unprompted or brings up this example of the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 然后他未经提示便主动提出了大屠杀这个例子。

sentences.en: And there's a set of people who deny that the Holocaust happened, right?
sentences.zh: 有一群人否认大屠杀曾经发生过，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, there's a lot.
sentences.zh: 是的，有很多人。

sentences.en: I find that deeply offensive.
sentences.zh: 我发现这深深地冒犯了我。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day,
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，

sentences.en: I don't believe that our platform should take that down because I think that there are things that different people get wrong.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们的平台应该删除这些内容，因为我认为不同的人会有不同的错误认知。

sentences.en: Either, I don't think that they're intentionally getting it wrong, but I think that they...
sentences.zh: 要么，我不认为他们是故意弄错的，但我认为他们……

sentences.en: In the case of the Holocaust deniers, they might be, but go ahead.
sentences.zh: 就大屠杀否认者而言，他们可能是故意的，但请继续。

sentences.en: It's hard to impugn intent and to understand the intent.
sentences.zh: 很难去质疑并理解他们的意图。

sentences.en: But I just think for as abhorrent as some of those examples are, I think the reality is also that
sentences.zh: 但我只是认为，尽管其中一些例子令人厌恶，但现实情况也是，

sentences.en: I get things wrong when I speak publicly.
sentences.zh: 我在公开讲话时也会犯错。

sentences.en: I'm sure you do.
sentences.zh: 我确信你也会。

sentences.en: I'm sure a lot of leaders and public figures who we respect do too.
sentences.zh: 我确信我们尊重的许多领导人和公众人物也是如此。

sentences.en: And I just don't think that it is the right thing to say we are going to take someone off the platform if they get things wrong
sentences.zh: 我只是认为，如果有人犯了错，我们就说要将他们赶出平台，这种做法是不对的，

sentences.en: even multiple times.
sentences.zh: 哪怕是多次犯错。

sentences.en: So he's essentially appealing to ideas that we've developed in our democracy over hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 所以他本质上是在呼吁我们在民主制度中经过几百年发展起来的理念。

sentences.en: I mean, he's saying that's the way we think about free speech is the way the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是在说我们看待言论自由的方式，就是美国

sentences.en: government thinks about free speech.
sentences.zh: 政府看待言论自由的方式。

sentences.en: There's no rule that that has to be the case.
sentences.zh: 没有任何规定说事情必须如此。

sentences.en: There's no reason he has to say we're going to draw the line on free speech here as opposed to somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 没有任何理由必须由他说“我们要在这里而不是在其他地方划定言论自由的界限”。

sentences.en: That's a choice that he's making, and I think that's sort of a way of avoiding the choice altogether is just to say, well, free speech is protected in the public sphere
sentences.zh: 这是他做出的选择，我认为这在某种程度上完全是在逃避选择，只需说，嗯，言论自由在公共领域受到保护，

sentences.en: so we're going to protect it in largely the same way on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将在脸书上以大致相同的方式保护它。

sentences.en: But Facebook can do whatever it wants.
sentences.zh: 但脸书可以随心所欲。

sentences.en: I mean, this is one thing that I think is broadly misunderstood about Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是我认为人们对脸书普遍存在误解的一点。

sentences.en: We speak about it as if it is a democracy, something that has to have a consistent set of values, that it applies equally to all of its users,
sentences.zh: 我们谈论它时，好像它是一个民主国家，是一个必须拥有一套一致的价值观、平等适用于所有用户、

sentences.en: and that there is some principle of fairness and equality that it must apply.
sentences.zh: 并且必须应用某种公平和平等原则的实体。

sentences.en: It's a company.
sentences.zh: 它是一家公司。

sentences.en: Facebook has no obligation to protect any particular kind of speech or ban any other kind of speech.
sentences.zh: 脸书没有义务保护任何特定类型的言论，也没有义务禁止任何其他类型的言论。

sentences.en: If they wanted to, they could say, well, if you deny that the Holocaust happened, we're going to lock you out and make you write an essay about the Holocaust
sentences.zh: 如果他们愿意，他们可以这样说：如果你否认大屠杀发生过，我们就把你锁在门外，让你写一篇关于大屠杀的文章，

sentences.en: until we find it acceptable and then we're going to let you back on.
sentences.zh: 直到我们觉得可以接受，然后我们再让你重新登录。

sentences.en: To be clear, I don't think they should do those things necessarily, but they could.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，我不认为他们非得做这些事情，但他们确实可以。

sentences.en: I mean, the point here is that Facebook has a ton of agency, but it is acting as if it's constrained by these American notions of free speech
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里的重点是，脸书拥有巨大的自主权，但它的行事方式却好像受到这些美国言论自由观念的束缚，

sentences.en: unless there's a reason to depart from them.
sentences.zh: 除非有理由背离它们。

sentences.en: I mean, there are certain things that Facebook is legally required to take down in certain countries.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某些国家，法律规定脸书必须删除某些特定内容。

sentences.en: So in countries like Germany, there are strict hate speech laws where you actually have to take down denials of the Holocaust and other types of hate speech,
sentences.zh: 所以在像德国这样的国家，有严格的仇恨言论法律，你实际上必须删除对大屠杀的否认和其他类型的仇恨言论，

sentences.en: or you're legally liable for that as a platform.
sentences.zh: 否则作为平台你将承担法律责任。

sentences.en: Facebook could be more like Germany if it wanted to.
sentences.zh: 如果脸书愿意，它可以变得更像德国。

sentences.en: But doing that would force Zuckerberg to make his power more known and more seen.
sentences.zh: 但这样做会迫使扎克伯格让他的权力更加显露、更加为人所见。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It would force him to be proactive rather than reactive.
sentences.zh: 这将迫使他采取主动，而不是被动作出反应。

sentences.en: Mark Zuckerberg wants to give power to other people, but he wants to make sure that they use that power responsibly.
sentences.zh: 马克·扎克伯格想要把权力赋予其他人，但他希望确保他们能负责任地使用这些权力。

sentences.en: And that's a really hard thing to do.
sentences.zh: 而这是一件非常难做到的事。

sentences.en: We've seen what happens when Facebook builds a thing and gives people the power to use it in whatever ways they want.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了当脸书打造了一个产品并赋予人们以他们想要的任何方式使用它的权力时会发生什么。

sentences.en: And it is really destructive.
sentences.zh: 而这确实具有破坏性。

sentences.en: And so now we're sort of asking him to accept the power that he has and to use it wisely.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有点在要求他接受他所拥有的权力并明智地使用它。

sentences.en: And I still think he's reluctant to do that.
sentences.zh: 而我依然认为他很不情愿这样做。

sentences.en: He still seems like he has accidentally put himself in the throne.
sentences.zh: 他看起来依然像是意外把自己推上了王位。

sentences.en: And now he is trying to give that back.
sentences.zh: 而现在他却想把责任推卸掉。

sentences.en: And we're saying, no, you can't do that.
sentences.zh: 而我们在说，不行，你不能这么做。

sentences.en: Like, you broke it, you buy it, you know?
sentences.zh: 就像是，你弄坏的，你就要买下来，对吧？

sentences.en: And like, that's...
sentences.zh: 而且感觉，那就是……

sentences.en: You make it, you own it.
sentences.zh: 你制造的，你就得承担。

sentences.en: Yeah, you make it, you own it.
sentences.zh: 对，你制造的，你就得承担。

sentences.en: And like, this is the fundamental tension that I think they're working through is whether he wants to or not,
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得，他们正在处理的根本矛盾在于，无论他愿不愿意，

sentences.en: Mark Zuckerberg has to solve this problem now that he's created.
sentences.zh: 马克·扎克伯格现在必须解决这个由他自己创造的问题。

sentences.en: And if he can't solve it, and if he's not willing to solve it, maybe he shouldn't have all this power.
sentences.zh: 如果他解决不了，如果他不愿意解决，也许他就不该拥有这么大的权力。

sentences.en: Maybe he shouldn't be in the position of getting to determine what is free and acceptable speech.
sentences.zh: 也许他不应该处于那个能够决定什么是自由且可接受的言论的地位。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kevin.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，凯文。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.zh: 回想当年我在黑胶时代的夜总会当DJ时，每晚你都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去上班，你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个充满活力的、由精美的50年历史藏品组成的快闪博物馆。

sentences.zh: 但如果能免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.zh: 周四，

sentences.en: White House Press Secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders announced that President Trump plans to invite President Putin to Washington for another meeting this fall.
sentences.zh: 白宫新闻秘书萨拉·赫卡比·桑德斯宣布，特朗普总统计划邀请普京总统今年秋天赴华盛顿进行另一次会晤。

sentences.zh: 插播一条突发新闻。

sentences.en: The White House has announced on Twitter that Vladimir Putin is coming to the White House in the fall.
sentences.zh: 白宫已在推特上宣布，弗拉基米尔·普京将于秋季访问白宫。

sentences.en: Trump's Director of National Intelligence,
sentences.zh: 特朗普的国家情报总监，

sentences.zh: 丹·科茨，是在一次会议的舞台上从NBC新闻主播安德里亚·米切尔那里得知这一邀请的。

sentences.zh: 再说一遍。

sentences.en: You...
Vladimir Putin coming to the...
sentences.zh: 弗拉基米尔·普京要来……

sentences.en: Did I hear you?
sentences.zh: 我没听错吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's going to be special.
sentences.zh: 那可真够特别的。

sentences.en: During the interview,
sentences.zh: 在采访中，

sentences.en: Coats acknowledged his frustration with the first meeting between Trump and Putin, especially the president's decision to speak with Putin without any aides present
sentences.zh: 科茨承认了他对特朗普和普京第一次会晤的挫败感，尤其是总统决定在没有任何助手在场的情况下与普京交谈

sentences.en: for nearly two hours.
sentences.zh: 将近两个小时。

sentences.en: If you had asked me how that ought to be conducted, I would have suggested a different way.
sentences.zh: 如果你问我那应该怎么进行，我会建议换一种方式。

sentences.en: But that's not my role.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是我的角色。

sentences.en: That's not my job.
sentences.zh: 这不是我的工作。

sentences.en: So, um, it is what it is.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
